name: Constellation Fund
blurb: Fights poverty across the Twin Cities by funding the region’s most effective local nonprofits.

name: Free Bikes 4 Kidz
blurb: Collects and refurbishes used bikes, then gives them to kids who need a set of wheels.

name: Appetite for Change
blurb: Uses food as a tool to build health, wealth, and community in North Minneapolis.

name: Feed My Starving Children
blurb: Volunteers hand-pack nutritious meals for malnourished kids around the world.

name: United Help Ukraine
blurb: Delivers humanitarian aid and medical supplies to Ukrainians affected by the war.

name: Agate Housing + Services
blurb: Works to prevent and end homelessness through shelter, housing, and food programs.

name: Save the Snakes
blurb: Protects snake populations and eases human–snake conflict through conservation and education.

name: Free Guitars 4 Kids
blurb: Puts guitars and music lessons into the hands of kids who want to play.

name: Oceanites
blurb: Studies Antarctic penguins and ecosystems to track the health of a warming planet.
reason: Penguins are their first priority, and they’re working to help a warming polar ecosystem.

name: Food Recovery Network
blurb: Rescues surplus food from 200+ college campuses to fight waste and feed communities.
reason: Started by 5 college students who saw good cafeteria food thrown away. Volunteers — I’m one! — pack the extras and send them to community food shelves.

name: Heart to Care Tanzania
blurb: Builds and grows a school in a small Tanzanian village, founded by a Twin Cities woman.
reason: Founded by a Twin Cities woman after a chance encounter in Tanzania. She works tirelessly to build and expand a village school and make sure everyone has what they need.

name: American Prairie
blurb: Building one of the largest nature reserves in America across the Montana prairie.
reason: I grew up on the prairie and have always been fascinated with bison and these ecosystems. I love what they’re doing to grow a thriving prairie.

name: SynGAP Research Fund
blurb: Funds research toward treatments and a cure for SYNGAP1-related disorders.
reason: I learned about SYNGAP1 through a YouTuber whose son has it — around 100 seizures a day. This fund researches the condition and supports families.

name: Water to Thrive
blurb: Builds wells bringing clean, safe water to communities across sub-Saharan Africa.
reason: 48% of people in sub-Saharan Africa lack clean water. They build wells — a single one can serve over 500 people for 20 years. Water should be a right, not a privilege.

name: Sprint to Cité Soleil
blurb: Empowers kids in Cité Soleil, Haiti through basketball, mentorship, and a meal.
reason: A Haiti nonprofit inspiring kids through basketball, mentorship, and a meal — founded by a teenager in our neighborhood.

name: World Central Kitchen
blurb: Serves fresh meals to communities in the wake of disasters worldwide.
reason: I first heard of them bringing meals to Ukraine. Chef José Andrés and WCK show up first after disasters. I’ve been very impressed.

name: Sandy Hook Promise
blurb: Works every day to protect children from gun violence — the leading cause of death for kids in America.
reason: A school shooting happened less than a mile from our home. Firearms are the leading cause of death for children and teens in America. Sandy Hook Promise is doing good work every day to stop it.

name: The Food Group
blurb: Gets local, healthy food to people in need and runs a sustainable teaching farm.
reason: So many people are food insecure. They get local, healthy food to people who need it — and run an organic farm teaching the next generation of sustainable farmers.

name: Border Angels
blurb: Supports migrants and refugees along the US–Mexico border with water, bond aid, and supplies.
reason: Centered around love, Border Angels help migrants and refugees along the US–Mexico border — water drops in the desert, bond support to reunite families, and supplies for people in need.

name: Animal Welfare Institute
blurb: Works to end human-caused suffering for animals everywhere — from labs to farms.
reason: Animals shouldn’t suffer because of humans. I think it’s our responsibility as a society to make sure we don’t make animals unnecessarily hurt.
